What's Different Here

Argent Forge is a fork of SLADE, for modding the games built on the Doom engine and the ports that run them. That covers Doom, Heretic, Hexen, Strife, Chex Quest and even Sonic Robo Blast 2, on ports from Boom and Eternity to ZDoom. Everything the original does it still does. What we put on top mostly reads DECORATE and ZScript, so it leans toward ZDoom and GZDoom, but the rest of the program is the same editor for anything in that family:

Actors

  • The Actor Constructor is a floating window that edits an actor's flags, properties and states, so most of DECORATE never has to be typed by hand. It applies changes as you make them, and every one of them can be undone.
  • It follows the text cursor: put the cursor anywhere inside an actor and that actor is the one you are editing.
  • A value field says what the engine wants there - INT, FLOAT or a quoted STRING - before you type it.
  • An Actions page lists the functions the engine has for states, and writes the call into your actor with its argument names already in it.
  • New actors and new script files can be created from the dialog, and the file is added to the archive's include list for you.
  • A thing number goes where its language reads it: the end of the DECORATE line, or MAPINFO for ZScript.
  • The Properties page has a divider you can drag to give the values room, and it remembers where you left it.

Code editor

  • Hovering a sprite frame in a state line pops up the picture it points at; hold SHIFT to run the whole state block as an animation.
  • A calltip shows a state action's arguments while you type, and resting on a flag or property name says what it does.
  • A script lump with no extension and no type is read as what its text says it is.

Image editor

  • Q picks up the brush and W the eraser - the Keyboard Shortcuts settings page points them at other keys.
  • Hold ALT and drag with the right button to change the brush size and how soft its edge is; ALT with the wheel changes how opaque it paints.
  • A brush picker for shape, size, feather and dither, and brush presets that are plain files you can send to someone.
  • Multiply and Screen blending for shadows and glow, and colour jitter for shading without reaching for the colour box.
  • SHIFT-click paints a straight line from wherever the last stroke ended, and Pixel perfect keeps a one-pixel diagonal one pixel thick.
  • The brush outline keeps following the pointer outside the picture, so a stroke starts where you see it starting.
  • Undo and redo cover the operations that used to go straight to disk, Convert to and the offsets among them.
  • The wheel can zoom around the cursor or around the middle of the picture instead of the corner it hangs from, for textures and sprites separately; pick it in the Image Editor settings.
  • Tile lays copies all the way around the original instead of only to its right and below, so every edge is on screen at once, and the number of copies each way is a setting.
  • In that view the picture loops under the brush: paint off the right edge and it comes back in on the left. That's how you make a seamless texture without moving pixels into place by hand.

General

  • A file carrying changes with no open tab is marked gold and italic in the entry tree, so nothing quietly stays unsaved.
  • The settings this build adds have their own branch of the preferences tree instead of being mixed in with SLADE's.
  • Two colour schemes of our own, Argent (Light) and Argent (Dark), sit beside SLADE's in the text editor's Colour Scheme menu. They are built on the four tones the art uses, and the start page goes dark or light with whichever one you pick.
  • This page and the archive tree are drawn in those tones too, so the tree's marks keep meaning what they always did: blue for edited, green for new, red for locked, gold for changed and left closed.
  • The version is our own line now rather than upstream's: this is 1.0.0, built on SLADE 3.2.12, which About says in those words. The flame over the hex is the program's mark on this page and in its icon.
